around.summary: The Times of India reports the blasts in an unlicensed storage shed near a school; ThePrint reports no casualties in a related cylinder blast on a vacant site. If you see cylinders stacked in a residential lane, report it to 112.

around.summary: The Times of India and NDTV report the student was called out of class and killed; ThePrint says it followed a clash between two groups. Parents and students should report campus-edge threats to the college and police early.

around.summary: Deccan Herald and The Hindu report the proposal, and The Times of India says fines for one-way violations and illegal parking may reach Rs 5,000 for repeat offenders. Habitual rule-breaking could soon cost you your licence.

street_smart.title: You wake up to a faint rotten-egg smell in your kitchen. Your phone shows the news of LPG cylinders blowing up near a school. You aren't sure whether the cylinder is leaking. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India / ThePrint: LPG cylinders explode in Bengaluru (2026-09-30).
street_smart.situation: The smell is faint but clear near the stove, and everyone is still asleep.

choices.text: Flip the light switch on to see where the leak is coming from.
choices.feedback: A switch can throw a tiny spark, and LPG ignites at low concentrations. Gas pools near the floor, so any spark, lighter or phone flashlight near the leak can set it off.

choices.text: Light a match near the regulator to check whether the gas is burning.
choices.feedback: This is the classic way leaks turn into fires. A leak is checked only with soapy water, never a flame.

choices.text: Turn the regulator off, open windows and doors, avoid switches, leave the kitchen and call your gas distributor's emergency number (1906) or 112.
choices.feedback: Closing the regulator stops the source, and ventilation disperses the heavier-than-air gas. Staying away from switches and flames removes ignition sources.

choices.text: Ignore it and re-check after tea.
choices.feedback: A leak in a closed room builds up concentration over time, so waiting only makes the explosive mix more likely.

takeaways: Check joints with soapy water, never a flame, and keep the regulator off at night.
Report stacked or unlicensed cylinders near homes or schools to 112.

quiz.question: What is the new licence system Karnataka plans, according to Deccan Herald?
quiz.why: Points-based systems add penalty points for each violation, and licences can be suspended once a threshold is crossed.

quiz.question: What did Krishna Byre Gowda order in response to Bengaluru's waterlogging?
quiz.why: Greater Bengaluru's civic administration is run through the GBA, which coordinates these response teams.

quiz.question: How much drug haul was seized from an Iranian boat, per The Times of India?
quiz.why: Such maritime seizures are typically made at sea by the Coast Guard and Navy working with narcotics agencies.

quiz.question: Which gas is the main component of household LPG?
quiz.why: LPG has no smell, so ethyl mercaptan is added to give it the rotten-egg odour that helps detect leaks.

quiz.question: Which of these is the emergency helpline number for all emergencies in India?
quiz.why: 112 is the unified emergency number; 108 is ambulance and 1098 is the child helpline.
